strings.d1.s0.name: Naama Bay Beach
strings.d1.s0.tips: The bay at the heart of town: hotel beaches and house-reef snorkelling (north end of the bay). Cooler in the morning.
strings.d1.s1.name: Naama Bay Promenade
strings.d1.s1.tips: Pedestrian promenade with cafes, shisha and shops where you haggle.
strings.d1.s2.name: Fares Seafood Naama
strings.d1.s2.tips: Sharm's famous seafood: pick from the counter, priced by weight. Try the Sinai calamari.
strings.d1.s3.name: Hotel Pool / Siesta
strings.d1.s3.tips: Pool and shade in the midday heat: the classic Red Sea beach routine.
strings.d1.s4.name: SOHO Square in the Evening
strings.d1.s4.tips: Dancing fountain, ice bar and Culturama: evening entertainment.
strings.d1.b0.name: El Masrien Grill Naama
strings.d1.b0.tips: Egyptian grill with kofta and chicken, a local favourite.
strings.d1.b1.name: Sharm Old Market in the Evening
strings.d1.b1.tips: The old market: spices, papyrus and haggling, plus Al Sahaba Mosque, lit up at night.
strings.d2.s0.name: Ras Mohammed National Park
strings.d2.s0.tips: At the tip of Sinai (30 minutes by boat or car), one of the world's best diving and snorkelling spots. Park fee about 15 USD.
strings.d2.s1.name: Shark Reef & Yolanda Reef Snorkelling
strings.d2.s1.tips: Wall reefs with Napoleon wrasse, barracuda and the toilets from the Yolanda shipwreck.
strings.d2.s2.name: Mangrove Channel & Enchanted Lagoon
strings.d2.s2.tips: A mangrove channel and a salty "magic lake" formed by an earthquake.
strings.d2.s3.name: Lunch on the Boat
strings.d2.s3.tips: Included in the tour: grilled fish and rice.
strings.d2.s4.name: Marsa Bareika Bay
strings.d2.s4.tips: A calm bay for snorkelling and beach time. Head back at 16:00.
strings.d2.b0.name: Ras Um Sid Reef
strings.d2.b0.tips: A headland reef inside the city (Hadaba). If you have no boat, enjoy the view from Farsha Cafe.
strings.d2.b1.name: Farsha Cafe Ras Um Sid
strings.d2.b1.tips: A clifftop cafe with Bedouin rugs, good for sunset and shisha.
strings.d3.s0.name: Mount Sinai Night Climb
strings.d3.s0.tips: 3 hours from Sharm (tour leaves at 22:00). Moses' Ten Commandments mountain, 2,285 m, with a camel path plus 750 steps, for sunrise. In winter it can drop to -5°C, so bring a heavy coat.
strings.d3.s1.name: Sunrise at the Summit Chapel
strings.d3.s1.tips: The Holy Trinity chapel, as Sinai's red mountains light up.
strings.d3.s2.name: Steps of Repentance Descent
strings.d3.s2.tips: 3,750 steps of the monks' path (Elijah's Basin). Hard on the knees.
strings.d3.s3.name: Saint Catherine's Monastery
strings.d3.s3.tips: A 6th-century UNESCO monastery (the oldest continuously active in the world): the Burning Bush, Moses' Well and icons. It may be closed Friday to Sunday.
strings.d3.s4.name: Bedouin Breakfast in St Catherine Village
strings.d3.s4.tips: Tea, bread and honey in a Bedouin tent. Head back at 15:00 (afternoon nap).
strings.d3.b0.name: Dahab Blue Hole
strings.d3.b0.tips: Instead of Sinai: snorkel at Dahab's legendary 100 m Blue Hole (the Bells), in a hippie town 1.5 hours away.
strings.d3.b1.name: Fox Camp St Catherine
strings.d4.s0.name: Tiran Island Boat Tour
strings.d4.s0.tips: 1 hour by boat from Sharm (tour about 50 USD). The island sits at the entrance to the Gulf of Aqaba and has 4 reefs (Jackson, Woodhouse, Thomas, Gordon).
strings.d4.s1.name: Jackson Reef Snorkelling
strings.d4.s1.tips: A colourful coral garden with turtles and the wreck of the Lara.
strings.d4.s2.name: Lunch on the Boat at Tiran
strings.d4.s3.name: Gordon Reef Swim
strings.d4.s3.tips: A shallow coral plateau where the Loullia wreck is visible. Head back at 15:30.
strings.d4.s4.name: Naama Bay Sunset Walk
strings.d4.s4.tips: Promenade and sea in the evening.
strings.d4.b0.name: White Island
strings.d4.b0.tips: A sandbar island that appears at low tide, as part of the Ras Mohammed tour.
strings.d4.b1.name: Camel Bar Naama
strings.d4.b1.tips: The rooftop bar of Camel Dive Club, with plenty of diver chat.
strings.d5.s0.name: Wadi Mandar Quad Safari
strings.d5.s0.tips: 1.5 hours by ATV/quad in the Sinai desert. Expect dust, so wear goggles.
strings.d5.s1.name: Bedouin Village Visit
strings.d5.s1.tips: Bedouin tea and bread baking, plus a short camel ride.
strings.d5.s2.name: Hotel Lunch & Siesta
strings.d5.s3.name: Desert Sunset & Stargazing Tour
strings.d5.s3.tips: Camels, a Bedouin dinner and stars through a telescope (no light pollution). Tour.
strings.d5.b0.name: Colored Canyon Nuweiba
strings.d5.b0.tips: A walk through a colourful rock canyon (2.5 hours' drive). A full day instead of the safari.
strings.d5.b1.name: Bedouin Dinner Camp
strings.d5.b1.tips: Lamb and rice, included in the tour.
strings.d6.s0.name: Discover Scuba Diving Naama
strings.d6.s0.tips: A trial dive (no certificate needed, 12 m with an instructor). Try Camel or Emperor Divers; Red Sea visibility is 30 m.
strings.d6.s1.name: Lunch at the Dive Centre Cafe
strings.d6.s2.name: Sharm Aquarium / Old Market
strings.d6.s2.tips: Afternoon at the market and Al Sahaba Mosque. Haggle.
strings.d6.s3.name: Al Fanar Ras Um Sid in the Evening
strings.d6.s3.tips: Italian seafood on the cliff, with the lighthouse and sunset.
strings.d6.b0.name: Dahab Lighthouse Reef & Town
strings.d6.b0.tips: A day in Dahab: Lighthouse snorkelling and beachfront cafes, 1.5 hours away.
strings.d6.b1.name: Hard Rock Cafe Naama
strings.d6.b1.tips: An evening alternative with live music.
strings.d7.s0.name: Shark's Bay Morning Snorkel
strings.d7.s0.tips: A bay close to the airport with a house reef and a jetty. One last swim.
strings.d7.s1.name: Hotel Breakfast
strings.d7.s1.tips: A long breakfast. Keep to cabin baggage.
strings.d7.s2.name: Sharm Old Market Souvenirs
strings.d7.s3.name: Sharm El Sheikh Airport
strings.d7.s3.tips: 15 minutes from Naama. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Il Mercato Hadaba
strings.d7.b0.tips: An open-air mall, as a alternative to the market.
strings.d7.b1.name: Tam Tam Naama Breakfast
strings.d7.b1.tips: Egyptian breakfast: ful (fava bean stew) and taameya (Egyptian falafel).
strings.note0: Haggle with taxis (Naama to Old Market 100-150 EGP) or use the hotel shuttle. Uber and Careem are limited. The airport is 15 minutes away. Tours pick you up from the hotel (Ras Mohammed, Tiran, Sinai, safari).
strings.note1: Summer is 38-42°C and dry; the sea is a wonderful 28°C. Stay by the pool or in the shade from 11:00 to 16:00 and snorkel at 7 in the morning. The Sinai night climb is cool.
strings.note2: Sinai visa: a free 15-day "Sinai only" stamp covers Sharm, Dahab and Sinai only; you cannot continue to Cairo. Turkish citizens pay 25 USD for an e-visa or on arrival.
strings.note3: Tour prices in USD: Ras Mohammed 40-60, Tiran 50, Sinai 40, safari 35-60, trial dive 90. Restaurants cost 200-400 EGP; tip (baksheesh) 20-50 EGP everywhere.
strings.note4: Do not step on the coral (you will be fined) and use reef-friendly sunscreen and water shoes. Resorts are relaxed for women, but dress modestly in the Old Market.
strings.note5: Try Sinai calamari, Egyptian breakfast (ful, taameya), koshari and umm ali dessert; alcohol is served in hotels.
